context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform by introducing a cloud-based web application for customers and adjusters. It ensures business continuity through a 3-year hybrid architecture that incrementally migrates claim types while synchronizing data with the on-premises legacy system.]

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers (Web users)
- Claims Adjusters (Internal web users)
- Modern Claims Platform (Azure West Europe, PaaS)
- Legacy Mainframe System (On-premises DB2/COBOL system of record)
- Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID (Identity Provider)
- Integration Middleware / API Gateway (Azure Service Bus / Azure Functions)

## Relationships
- End Customers and Brokers interact with Modern Claims Platform via HTTPS/REST for claim submission (R-01)
- Claims Adjusters interact with Modern Claims Platform via HTTPS/REST for claim handling (R-02)
- Modern Claims Platform authenticates users against Corporate Active Directory via OIDC/SAML (R-07)
- Modern Claims Platform synchronizes data with Legacy Mainframe via secure message queues and APIs over hybrid IPsec VPN/ExpressRoute with mTLS
- Modern Claims Platform accesses secrets securely via Azure Key Vault using Azure Managed Identities

## Technology Stack
- Microsoft Azure West Europe: Managed cloud platform chosen to offset the team's low cloud experience and reduce operational overhead
- Azure App Service & Azure Functions: Serverless and PaaS containers for hosting UI and integration logic to guarantee sub-2s adjuster response times (R-05)
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging to respect the rigid 23:00-05:00 nightly batch window and ensure lossless consistency (R-04)
- Azure SQL Database: Managed database with AES-256 encryption for cached claims data and state management
- Azure Key Vault & Managed Identities: Centralized credential management preventing hardcoded secrets across the hybrid boundary

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture decouples the modern user interface from legacy mainframe latency, satisfying performance and security requirements. It enables risk-free incremental migration and rapid 1-day rollbacks through isolated routing logic and managed asynchronous integration.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a cloud-based hybrid Modern Claims Platform that modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system. It enables gradual claim type migration while ensuring business continuity and zero data loss.

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers [person]
- Claims Adjusters [person]
- Migration Operations Managers [person]
- Customer Web Portal [container, SPA/React]
- Adjuster Web Application [container, Modular Monolith/.NET]
- Migration Operations Dashboard [container, Web App/.NET]
- Claims Core API Service [container, Modular Monolith/.NET]
- Claim Router & Integration Worker [container, .NET Worker Service]
- Modern Claims Platform [softwareSystem]
- Legacy Mainframe System [externalSystem]
- Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID [externalSystem]
- Integration Middleware / API Gateway [externalSystem]
- Azure Service Bus [container]

## Relationships
- End Customers and Brokers -> Customer Web Portal via HTTPS/REST
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web Application via HTTPS/REST
- Migration Operations Managers -> Migration Operations Dashboard via HTTPS/REST
- Modern Claims Platform -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID via OIDC/SAML
- Claim Router & Integration Worker -> Legacy Mainframe System via mTLS/VPN and signed JWT
- Claims Core API -> Azure Service Bus via AMQP

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts the modular monolith web applications and core APIs to reduce operational complexity
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the React customer portal
- Azure Container Apps / App Service: Hosts the .NET Worker Service for asynchronous routing
- Azure Service Bus: Manages messaging, backpressure, dead-letter queues, and rate-limiting
- Azure Application Insights: Provides distributed tracing and observability across the hybrid boundary
- Azure Key Vault & Managed Identities: Secures credentials, secrets, and service-to-service authentication
- Bicep / Terraform: Automates Infrastructure-as-Code and blue-green deployments via Azure Deployment Slots

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates asynchronous mainframe integration from synchronous web requests using a modular monolith and worker pattern, ensuring adjuster screens load in under two seconds despite slow legacy response times. Furthermore, per-claim-type feature flagging and versioned IaC pipelines guarantee the strict one-day emergency fallback and zero data loss requirements.

Customer Web Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Customer Web Portal is a React-based single-page application enabling end customers and brokers to submit and manage claims. It integrates with Azure Container Apps and Azure Static Web Apps to modernize access while supporting gradual backend migration.

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers
- Customer Web Portal (SPA/React)
- Authentication Component (TypeScript/MSAL.js)
- Claim Submission Form Component (React/Formik)
- Claim Status & Dashboard Component (React)
- API Gateway Client Component (Axios/Fetch)
- Resilience & Fallback Component
- Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID
- Claims Core API Service (Modular Monolith/.NET)
- Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- End Customers and Brokers -> Customer Web Portal: Accesses portal UI [HTTPS/REST]
- Customer Web Portal -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID: Authenticates users [OIDC/SAML]
- Claim Submission Form Component -> API Gateway Client Component: Sends claim payload [HTTPS/REST]
- Customer Web Portal (Components) -> Claims Core API Service: Submits and retrieves claim data via BFF [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway Client Component -> Azure Application Insights: Tracks frontend performance and errors [RUM/Telemetry]

## Technology Stack
- React / TypeScript: Frontend framework for dynamic UI rendering and component architecture
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) Pattern: Secures token handling and eliminates browser local storage risks
- Azure Static Web Apps & Azure Container Apps: Hosts static assets and BFF services for operational simplicity
- Azure Application Insights: Provides real user monitoring (RUM) and synthetic transaction logging
- MSAL.js: Implements authentication flows with OIDC/SAML protocols

## Rationale
This component architecture secures user sessions via a BFF pattern, shielding a cloud-inexperienced team from token management risks. It dynamically adapts UI components to support gradual claim type migrations without disrupting users.

Adjuster Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
The Adjuster Web Application modernizes claim handling for internal users within a hybrid cloud architecture. It provides a sub-2-second responsive interface while integrating with a legacy mainframe system.

## Key Elements
- Claims Adjusters (Person)
- Adjuster UI (SPA/React Component)
- Claim Handling API (ASP.NET Core Component)
- Claim Context & Routing Component (.NET Component)
- Mainframe Abstraction Layer (.NET Component)
- Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID (External System)
- Claims Core API Service (Container)

## Relationships
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster UI: Manage claims [HTTPS/REST]
- Adjuster UI -> Claim Handling API: Invoke workflows [HTTPS/REST]
- Claim Handling API -> Claim Context & Routing Component: Evaluate routing [In-Memory]
- Claim Context & Routing Component -> Mainframe Abstraction Layer: Fetch fallback data [In-Memory]
- Claim Handling API -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID: Authenticate users [OIDC/OAuth 2.0]

## Technology Stack
- SPA/React: Provides responsive adjuster screens with optimistic updates
- ASP.NET Core: Powers the modular monolith backend API
- Azure Container Apps: Simplifies cloud deployment for a team with low cloud experience
- Azure App Configuration: Implements feature flags for rapid 1-day claim type rollbacks

## Rationale
The CQRS and caching patterns insulate user screens from slow legacy mainframe responses to meet the sub-2-second load requirement. Feature flags and decoupled routing allow individual claim types to be safely rolled back to the mainframe within one day.

Migration Operations Dashboard.analysis:
## Overview
- This system modernizes a regional insurer's legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform using a hybrid cloud architecture.
- It provides a modern web interface for customers, brokers, and adjusters while maintaining business continuity through a gradual, claim-type-by-claim-type migration.

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Migration Operations Managers
- Modern Claims Platform
- Customer Web Portal (SPA/React)
- Adjuster Web Application (Modular Monolith/.NET)
- Migration Operations Dashboard (Web App/.NET)
- Claims Core API Service (Modular Monolith/.NET)
- Claim Router & Integration Worker (.NET Worker Service)
- Azure Service Bus (Azure Messaging Service)
- Legacy Mainframe System
- Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID

## Relationships
- End Customers and Brokers -> Customer Web Portal [HTTPS/REST]
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web Application [HTTPS/REST]
- Migration Operations Managers -> Migration Operations Dashboard [HTTPS/REST]
- Customer Web Portal -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID [OIDC/SAML]
- Adjuster Web Application -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID [OIDC/SAML]
- Migration Operations Dashboard -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID [OIDC/SAML]
- Migration Operations Dashboard -> Claims Core API Service [HTTPS/REST, TLS 1.3, JWT]
- Claims Core API Service -> Azure Service Bus [AMQP]
- Claim Router & Integration Worker -> Legacy Mainframe System [mTLS/VPN and signed JWT]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts web applications in `azure-westeurope` to support the team's familiarity level.
- ASP.NET Core (.NET): Used for backend services and the Migration Operations Dashboard to maintain architectural consistency.
- Azure Service Bus: Manages messaging, backpressure, and dead-letter queues.
- Azure Active Directory / Entra ID: Provides Single Sign-On, MFA, and RBAC enforcement.
- Azure Monitor and Application Insights: Handles centralized logging, telemetry, and alerting.

## Rationale
- The hybrid architecture keeps the legacy mainframe as the system of record to minimize expensive legacy modifications.
- The modular services and dedicated migration dashboard ensure strict consistency, auditability, and the ability to roll back claim types within one day.

- Azure Service Bus (Azure Messaging Service)

- End Customers and Brokers -> Customer Web Portal (HTTPS/REST)

- Migration Operations Dashboard -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID (OIDC/SAML)

## Technology Stack
- React: Powers the Customer Web Portal for responsive claim submissions.
- .NET: Used for backend containers (Modular Monolith / Worker Services) to ensure high maintainability and performance.
- Azure Service Bus: Manages asynchronous messaging, backpressure, and dead-letter queues.
- Entity Framework Core with Azure SQL: Maintains local read models for sub-2-second adjuster response times.
- Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID: Handles Single Sign-On via OIDC/SAML.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture allows gradual migration of claim types while keeping the mainframe as the system of record. Local read models and anti-corruption layers isolate users from mainframe latency and enable rapid one-day rollbacks.]

Claim Router & Integration Worker.analysis:
## Overview
The Claim Router & Integration Worker is an asynchronous .NET service that routes and integrates claims between the cloud platform and the legacy mainframe. It ensures seamless, secure hybrid operations while claim types are gradually migrated over a three-year period.

## Key Elements
- Claim Router & Integration Worker (.NET Worker Service)
- Routing Engine Component (.NET class library)
- Mainframe Adapter Component (.NET HttpClient/gRPC)
- Outbox Processor Component (.NET Hosted Service)
- Audit & Telemetry Component (Application Insights)
- Azure Service Bus (Azure Messaging Service)
- Legacy Mainframe System (On-premises DB2/COBOL)
- Azure Key Vault (Secret Management)

## Relationships
- Claim Router & Integration Worker -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)
- Claim Router & Integration Worker -> Legacy Mainframe System (mTLS and signed JWT over hybrid IPsec VPN)
- Claim Router & Integration Worker -> Azure Key Vault (HTTPS/Managed Identity)
- Routing Engine Component -> Claims Core API Service Database (HTTPS/SQL)

## Technology Stack
- .NET Worker Service: Chosen for robust asynchronous processing and native integration with Azure services.
- Azure Container Apps: Provides simple, scalable container hosting suitable for teams with limited cloud experience.
- Azure Service Bus: Manages messaging, backpressure, and reliable queueing to prevent duplicate or lost claims.
- Azure Key Vault: Secures sensitive mTLS certificates and signing keys using managed identities.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees zero data loss and supports rapid one-day rollbacks through an outbox pattern and dynamic routing rules. It safely bridges the cloud and the legacy mainframe while accommodating the team's limited cloud experience.

Azure Service Bus.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform designed to gradually replace a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe while maintaining continuous claims processing. It provides secure, scalable web applications for customers, brokers, and adjusters while ensuring strict data consistency and seamless fallback capabilities.]

## Key Elements
- Modern Claims Platform [softwareSystem]
- End Customers and Brokers [person]
- Claims Adjusters [person]
- Migration Operations Managers [person]
- Legacy Mainframe System [externalSystem]
- Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID [externalSystem]
- Integration Middleware / API Gateway [externalSystem]
- Customer Web Portal (SPA/React) [container]
- Adjuster Web Application (Modular Monolith/.NET) [container]
- Migration Operations Dashboard (Web App/.NET) [container]
- Claims Core API Service (Modular Monolith/.NET) [container]
- Claim Router & Integration Worker (.NET Worker Service) [container]
- Azure Service Bus (Azure Messaging Service) [container]
  - Topic Router Component [component]
  - Session Manager Component [component]
  - Dead-Letter Monitor Component [component]
  - Claim Message Schema Registry Component [component]
  - Backpressure & Throttling Controller Component [component]

## Relationships
- End Customers and Brokers -> Customer Web Portal (HTTPS/REST)
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Web Application (HTTPS/REST)
- Migration Operations Managers -> Migration Operations Dashboard (HTTPS/REST)
- Customer Web Portal -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID (OIDC/SAML)
- Adjuster Web Application -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID (OIDC/SAML)
- Migration Operations Dashboard -> Corporate Active Directory / Entra ID (OIDC/SAML)
- Claim Router & Integration Worker -> Legacy Mainframe System (mTLS/VPN and signed JWT)
- Claims Core API Service -> Azure Service Bus (AMQP)
- Claims Core API Service -> Claim Message Schema Registry Component (AMQP)
- Claim Message Schema Registry Component -> Topic Router Component (Internal memory/pipelining)
- Topic Router Component -> Claim Router & Integration Worker (AMQP via Azure Service Bus Subscriptions)
- Topic Router Component -> Session Manager Component (AMQP)
- Session Manager Component -> Claim Router & Integration Worker (AMQP)

## Technology Stack
- Azure Service Bus Premium Tier: Selected for geo-disaster recovery, VNet service endpoints, and auto-inflate capabilities to handle high throughput securely.
- .NET (Modular Monolith & Worker Services): Chosen for core backend logic and asynchronous claim routing due to robust enterprise capabilities.
- React (SPA): Used for interactive, modern customer and broker portal interfaces.
- Microsoft Entra ID (RBAC) with Managed Identities: Replaces SAS keys to enforce least-privilege security across all microservices.
- Terraform: Enforces Infrastructure-as-Code for consistent, automated, and drift-free deployments.
- Azure Key Vault: Manages Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) for encryption at rest and automated key rotation.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture bridges the legacy on-premises COBOL/DB2 mainframe with modern cloud services by leveraging Azure Service Bus as a reliable buffer to prevent data loss and enforce backpressure during strict batch windows. It mitigates the team's low cloud experience through managed Azure components and automated infrastructure deployment while fulfilling all regulatory, performance, and gradual migration constraints.]
